dernierCall.guidanceProchainTrimestre: No quantified quarterly guidance (Q3 is a revenue-only release, due October 21, 2026 post-market close; quiet period starts September 22). Qualitatively, early July traded in line with a soft June then improved slightly; management explicitly declined to extrapolate current trading. Space contribution ran slightly below the ~4% FY pace in Q2, judged not meaningful on a quarterly basis.
dernierCall.guidanceAnnuelle: No quantified FY revenue or EPS target. Long-standing ambition to protect a group EBIT margin 'in the region of 29%+' reiterated, explicitly conditional on H2 top-line delivery (H2 called the most important half of the year). FY26 operating parameters confirmed: governance one-off ~EUR 2M in H2 (vs EUR 8M in H1, ~EUR 10M FY), net capex back to ~6% of revenue by year-end, marketing ~7% of revenue, space contribution ~4%, year-end NWC back to ~9.7% of revenue. Early 2027 indications: space again ~4%, price increases low-to-mid single digit at current input costs and FX.
pointsCles: Sharp Q2 deceleration (group revenue +5% cFX vs +12% cFX in Q1), with Moncler EMEA down 8% cFX on collapsing Asian and American tourist inflows to Europe - most acute in June - and a weak European online channel; Asia held at +12% as demand repatriated to local markets (Chinese cluster still up double digit, Korea ~10% of group revenue and strong locally).

Management flags an intensifying 'Buy Now, Wear Now' behavior across all regions (customers purchasing in-season rather than pre-buying Fall/Winter), delaying part of H2 demand; the first-ever end-to-end Spring/Summer push ('Have a Puffy Summer') performed well through April-June and early July and is framed as a structural multi-season commitment, not a one-off campaign.

First earnings call for new Group CEO Leo (Bartolomeo) Rongone (in post since April 1, 2026, Remo Ruffini executive chairman): stated priorities are US relevance, an all-season customer dialogue, the three Moncler brand dimensions (Collection, Grenoble, Genius) and deeper, more personal VIC engagement - continuity, no strategy reset; the EUR 8M H1 governance one-off (~EUR 10M FY) stems from this transition.

H1 EBIT margin 19.0% (18.3% LY; ~19.6% ex one-off) on strict cost control and favorable channel mix (gross margin 77.2%); Stone Island posted a fourth straight double-digit quarter (+11% cFX, DTC +15%) on volume plus category mix (outerwear/knitwear vs entry price), and the NY Fifth Avenue flagship (opening September 2026, rent already expensed) is the pivotal H2 milestone for the US bet.

hypothese.summary: The Moncler/Stone Island duo still at ~1,1 Md EUR of net cash, but Q2 in marked deceleration (+5% cFX vs +12% in Q1) on the back of European tourism; management transition (CEO Rongone, Ruffini executive chairman) under way, Asia/Stone Island thesis reiterated with no material revision to the core of the projection.
hypothese.text:
== THESIS SUMMARY ==
Two functional-luxury brands: Moncler (~84% of H1 revenue) and Stone Island (~16%), EBIT margin ~29-30%, net cash 1.11bn (ex-lease debt). The thesis rests on Asian demand resilience, Stone Island's ramp (4th consecutive double-digit quarter) and the American bet (New York flagship, September 2026). Q2 decelerated sharply (+5% cFX vs +12% in Q1), with Moncler EMEA -8% cFX on weak European tourism - the buy-now-wear-now dynamic sharpens seasonality.

== THESIS READ ==
- The Q2 deceleration is tourism-flow driven (EMEA), not brand-heat loss: Asia held and Stone Island compounds. Watch: Q3 print - the first cold-season indicator and flagship NY opening effect.
- Stone Island is graduating from turnaround to growth engine - divergent segment dynamics now explicit in the model. Watch: SI wholesale-to-retail mix milestones.
- The US bet concentrates 2027 upside (flagship NY, Sept 2026 opening). Watch: opening reception and US DTC comps.

== SPECIAL FACTORS ==
Financial result deviates from the standard E5-a bis cash-yield rule: it is structurally dominated by IFRS16 lease interest, RISING with network expansion (flagship NY) - projected on the observed lease trajectory (ancrage resultat_financier_ifrs16). Governance one-off (~2M) reintegrated. Shares flat (no buyback; growing dividend policy). ETR 29.4% normative.

== PARAMETERS & WATCH-LIST ==
2026: revenue 3,273M (+4.5%), EBIT 970M (29.6%), EPS 2.44; 2027-2030: ~6.5%/yr revenue, gradual margin expansion (marge_expansion_graduelle), net cash building to 2.05bn. Watch: Grenoble/Olympics momentum normalization (reconducted, undetailed this quarter); flagship NY execution; European tourism flows; JV/governance evolutions.

== CATALYSTS ==
Q3 revenue (Oct); flagship NY opening (Sept); cold-season sell-through; FY26 results (Feb 2027).

ancrages.moteur: Confirmed Q2 slowdown (group revenue +5% cFX vs +12% cFX in Q1, Moncler EMEA -8% cFX) tied to the decline in European tourism and to 'buy now wear now' behaviour; H2 2026 revenue is modelled with a further deceleration of the reported pace (~+4% vs H2 2025) rather than a re-acceleration, contrary to the implicit assumption of the Q1 thesis.

One-off of 8 M EUR (H1) / ~10 M EUR (full year) tied to the new governance structure (CEO/board transition), treated as a genuine one-off and stripped out of the normative EBIT margin (ex-one-off, underlying H1 margin ~19,6% vs 19,0% reported).

The group net financial result remains structurally negative despite a net cash position (excluding lease debt) because of interest on IFRS16 lease liabilities (25,0 M EUR in H1 2026, rising with the expansion of the network, notably the New York flagship); the standard Bund+2pts yield rule on net cash (E5-a bis, the cash case with no documented active buyback) is set aside in favour of a projection anchored on the observed trajectory of lease charges.

Gradual EBIT margin expansion at the historical pace (+30 to 40 bps/yr), driven by the growing DTC mix of both brands and by the ramp-up of Stone Island, moderated beyond management's long-term ambition in the 29%+ area (already reached in 2025 at 29,2%) for want of a higher quantified target.
Normative tax rate maintained at 29,4%, stable and consistent across FY2024/FY2025/H1 2026 (29,7%/29,4%/29,4%), with no one-off item identified.

Dividend projected in line with net income growth (FY2025 dividend of 1,40 EUR/share, 374,1 M EUR paid in May 2026, the starting base for the net cash trajectory); no documented regular buyback programme (treasury shares stable at ~1% of the share capital), hence the absence of a nil yield on net cash in the normative financial result calculation (see anchor resultat_financier_ifrs16).

Stone Island (16% of H1 revenue, 4th consecutive quarter of double-digit growth, +11% cFX in Q2 and over H1) continues to grow markedly faster than the Moncler brand (+9% in H1 but only +3% cFX in Q2); the group mix incorporates a slightly rising Stone Island share over the projection horizon, without extrapolating its current pace indefinitely.

Opening of the Fifth Avenue flagship in New York in September 2026: cost impact (rent/staff) already partly incorporated in 2026 selling expenses, with a significant contribution to revenue and to sales density expected from 2027, without any major leverage on the 2026 projections.

clesRetenues: Q Natasha Bonnet (Morgan Stanley) - price/volume mix and intra-quarter trend: management confirms that price predominated in Q2 (volumes flat to slightly negative, against positive volumes in Q1); quarter described as "good, not excellent" - April/May very good, June markedly weaker on the back of declining traffic across all regions.

Q Anne-Laure Bismuth (HSBC) - Q2 space contribution and US slowdown: management never discloses the space contribution by quarter (judged not significant), maintains the ~4% annual target; the US slowdown attributed to lower wholesale shipments (Saks Global in Chapter 11), with US DTC still above the 4% group average.

Q Anne-Laure Bismuth (HSBC) - a Genius-type event tied to the New York flagship opening: no specific format confirmed, described as a continuous multi-channel 'offensive' rather than a one-off event, with management explicitly dismissing the idea of a single 'magic wand'.

Q Luca Solca (Bernstein) - why the tourists lost in Europe are not recaptured elsewhere: management confirms that they are probably buying locally, a partial explanation for the strength in Asia (+12%, driven by China/Korea).

Q Luca Solca (Bernstein) - Rongone's first impressions (3 months) and improvement areas identified: the new CEO cites an opportunity to strengthen direct and personalised engagement with VICs (the most important clients), with no other specific criticism voiced at this stage.

Q Daria Nasledysheva (BofA) - FY margin outlook vs consensus (only +10 bps modelled): management explicitly declines to give an outlook, profitability depending entirely on H2 revenue (the most important half of the year); ~29%+ ambition reiterated without further precision.
Q Daria Nasledysheva (BofA) - current trend July vs June: early July in line with June then slightly better; management explicitly declines any more precise comment on the last few days' results.

Q Oriana Cardani (Intesa Sanpaolo) - share of new customers at Moncler/Stone Island and 2027 space/price guidance: ~50% of Moncler revenue comes from new customers (60% by customer count, loyal customers spending more); 2027 space still ~4% (indicative), price low to mid single digit (still premature).

Q Melania Grippo (BNP Paribas) - online channel weakness and spring/summer delivery cadence: online weakness concentrated in Europe only (other regions in line with or above physical); intention to spread spring/summer coverage over a longer part of the season next year, rather than concentrating it at the start of the season.

Q Erwan Rambourg (Goldman Sachs) - cost impact of the New York flagship on the H2 cost base and other major H2 projects: costs (rent+staff) already incorporated in selling expenses from the signing of the lease, regardless of the opening date; no quantification given, no other major H2 project flagged beyond New York.

Q Erwan Rambourg (Goldman Sachs) - weight and nature of the growth in Korea: Korea ~10% of group revenue, solid growth off a high comparison base, high sales density; not an isolated case, Asian growth judged broad and not concentrated in Korea alone.

Q Charles-Louis Scotti (Kepler Cheuvreux) - Stone Island's EMEA underperformance and acceleration of store openings: EMEA weaker across the whole luxury sector at present, ongoing curation of the wholesale network (deliberate closures); no major 2027 opening plan, priority given to organic growth and sales density before accelerating.

Q Charles-Louis Scotti (Kepler Cheuvreux) - renewal of the Inter Parfums fragrance licence (expiring December 2026) and the possibility of a broader partnership with a player such as L'Oreal: RENEWAL DECISION ON HOLD, under evaluation; selectivity strategy reaffirmed, no move towards a large beauty player confirmed at this stage.

Q Carole Madjo (Barclays) - spring/summer vs fall/winter product mix in store in Q2 and the economics of the collection (basket, density): SS predominant in April/May, FW pre-delivered from June onwards; economics not detailed but a good SS conversion rate observed and specifically tracked.

Q Carole Madjo (Barclays) - origin and geographic extent of the 'buy now, wear now' behaviour: management corrects the terminology (not 'see now buy now') and confirms that this behaviour is observed IN ALL MARKETS, with a more marked impact in Europe owing to its combination with the decline in tourism.

Q Chris Gao (CLSA) - will 'buy now wear now' shift FW demand into H2, and inventory preparation for the high season: management plays it down, foresees no radical change in the way it is managed, will continue to rely on the existing core business while gradually broadening the seasonal offer.

Q Chris Gao (CLSA) - volume/price-mix breakdown of Stone Island's DTC growth and margin trajectory: growth = volumes AND a mix effect towards higher-priced categories (knitwear/outerwear vs entry-level sweatshirts/T-shirts), no significant standalone price increase; profitability set to improve with continued organic growth and sales density still below target.

Q Jean Bossy (Oddo BHF) - historical split of Q2/Q3 sales between spring/summer and fall/winter: not disclosed in detail by quarter, but confirmed at ~25% SS / 75% FW for the full 2025 year, with the SS share rising slightly sequentially over several years.

Q James Grzinic (Jefferies) - share of the network that benefited from the full spring/summer assortment: collection rolled out across the whole network, but the full immersive experience (layering system) reserved for a limited share of stores - a learning approach, with gradual extension planned season after season, no precise percentage given.

Q Paola Carboni (Equita SIM) - apparent contradiction between Korea cited as a DTC driver and the Korean cluster being 'flat': explained by strong local consumption offsetting fewer Korean tourists travelling to Europe (vs Q1) - the CLUSTER (nationality) and the MARKET (geography) tell two different stories.
Q Paola Carboni (Equita SIM) - teaser on the Q4 initiatives: confidence expressed on the H2 plans in continuity with previous years, no concrete detail disclosed.

Q Piral Dadhania (RBC) - why the gross margin did not benefit more from the positive regional/channel mix: the improvement attributed PURELY to channel mix, no other material factor identified (markup and obsolescence provisions stable, marginally negative FX effect).

Q Piral Dadhania (RBC) - was the level of risk-taking on spring/summer inventory insufficient (out-of-stocks in store): management explicitly CONFIRMS having preferred a calculated risk (even at the cost of being 'short' on certain items) rather than over-stocking, given the unprecedented nature of the first full SS year.

Q Thomas Chauvet (Citi) - growth pace of the Chinese cohort in Q2 (vs +20% in Q1) and onshore/offshore split: Chinese cluster still double-digit in Q2 (decelerating vs Q1), no notable onshore/offshore difference flagged.

Q Chiara Battistini (JPMorgan) - trajectory of operating costs in H2 and nature of the New York costs (rent already included, only staff still to come): no material acceleration in costs expected in H2 beyond the items already known (governance one-off brought down to ~2 M EUR); confirms that the NY rent is already booked ahead of the opening, with only staff still to ramp up.

Q Chiara Battistini (JPMorgan) - implicit sign of the Q2 like-for-like given the 7% in H1: management qualitatively confirms a 'slightly positive' Q2 LFL, the space contribution having been slightly negative (online weakness).
